extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary authors, and readers interested in poetic theory (esp. Romantic-era poets and critics)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on composing poetry that balances fidelity to nature and imaginative novelty, distinguishing imagination from fancy, choosing subjects (supernatural vs ordinary), and selecting appropriate diction and terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to excite sympathy by faithful adherence to the truth of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: One cardinal point of poetry is 'the power of exciting the sympathy of the reader by a faithful adherence to the truth of nature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select incidents, characters, and emotions true to human experience so readers' sympathy is engaged; this is the route to realistic poetic effect. Example/contrast: poems drawn from ordinary life should use situations and characters 'such as will be found in every village' to excite sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of giving novelty via the modifying colours of imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: The other cardinal point is 'the power of giving the interest of novelty by the modifying colours of imagination.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use imaginative modification (tone, imagery, perspective) to make familiar material feel new. This is complementary to fidelity: combine truth of nature with imaginative novelty to produce poetic interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of subject: supernatural versus ordinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Poems may be of two sorts: (1) incidents/agents supernatural (or romantic) treated so as to produce human interest; (2) subjects chosen from ordinary life to yield novelty and awaken attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For supernatural subjects, present the dramatic truth of emotions that would accompany such situations to secure a willing suspension of disbelief ('poetic faith'). For ordinary subjects, direct attention to the loveliness in everyday objects and experiences to evoke wonder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce 'poetic faith' by dramatizing plausible emotions in supernatural contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: When supernatural elements are used, the excellence aimed at 'is to consist in the interesting of the affections by the dramatic truth of such emotions, as would naturally accompany such situations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray emotions and reactions with credible human feeling so the reader temporarily accepts the supernatural; avoid mere sensationalism—sustain 'willing suspension of disbelief' through verisimilitude in feeling and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish imagination from fancy (transformative vs associative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagination is primary/secondary and a 'living power' that re-creates and idealizes; Fancy is 'a mode of memory emancipated from the order of time and space' and works by associative aggregation of ready-made materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use imagination to dissolve, diffuse and re-create (transform reality into new unified forms). Use fancy when you need associative, memory-based combinations and decorative imagery. Avoid mistaking associative aggregation for true imaginative creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary imagination as the formative, creative faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary imagination is 'the living power and prime agent of all human perception, and as a repetition in the finite mind of the eternal act of creation in the infinite I am.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the imagination as formative: it unifies and gives life to perception. In practice, foreground original, synthetic acts of mind rather than mere recombination of images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate diction: use of the language of ordinary life (with caveats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wordsworth proposed using 'the language of real life'—Coleridge records that the Lyrical Ballads aimed to manage subjects 'in the language of ordinary life' to produce interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain/daily language can make poetry more immediate and produce sympathy; but consider context and audience—some passages may demand loftier diction or philosophical density. Avoid unexpected abstruse disquisitions in a miscellany without clear reader preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid methodless eclecticism; maintain system and logical connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the 'predominance of a popular philosophy' and 'methodical aphoristic Eclectics' who 'dismiss not only all system, but all logical connection' and pick and choose whatever is showy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build poems and collections with internal coherence and logical design rather than assembling attractive but disconnected fragments. Anti-pattern: superficial, showy phrases that disguise lack of thought or system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use technical or new coinages only to prevent confusion and assist memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify technical terms 'whenever they tend to preclude confusion of thought, and when they assist the memory by the exclusive singleness of their meaning.' Unusual words are an evil if they produce vagueness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coin terms only when necessary to clarify concepts; prefer clear expression otherwise. Risk: overuse of learned jargon substitutes ostentation for clear conception and may alienate readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be precise in terminology; avoid vague, indefinite nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Coleridge criticizes vague terms used in metaphysical schools and argues that errors 'cannot subsist, except as they are concealed behind the mask of a plausible and indefinite nomenclature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define key poetic/critical terms clearly to prevent misunderstanding. Vagueness can hide conceptual errors and impede the reader's ability to follow argument or poetic method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match abstruseness and depth to audience expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not surprise readers with abstruse metaphysical disquisition in an unexpected context; readers of a 'miscellaneous poems' volume may rightly complain if a long metaphysical chapter is included without warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing poetry alongside theoretical or philosophical material, signal the nature and depth of that material (e.g., reserve dense treatises for a separate, announced work) to avoid alienating readers unprepared for abstruse content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of tools: know distinct roles of fancy and imagination in composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A man may 'work with two very different tools at the same moment; each has its share in the work, but the work effected by each is distinct and different.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consciously deploy fancy (associative imagery, memory) and imagination (transformative synthesis) for their appropriate effects; do not blur their functions or attribute to one what belongs to the other.
